claims.text: On 17 May 2026 the WHO Director-General determined that the epidemic of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the DRC and Uganda constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

WHO Disease Outbreak News #613 (17 July 2026): as of 15 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported 2,124 confirmed cases including 828 deaths (case fatality ratio 39%), with Ituri province the most affected (27 of 36 health zones; 89.6% of cases, 83.6% of deaths), and further cases in North Kivu (11 of 34 health zones), South Kivu (1 of 34 health zones), Haut-Uele (4 of 13 health zones) and Tshopo (3 of 23 health zones). As of 17 July 2026, Uganda reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths in imported cases plus one probable case resulting in death. WHO assessed the risk as very high nationally in DRC due to ongoing transmission and expansion into new health zones, high in Uganda due to confirmed cross-border spread, high for countries sharing land borders with the affected countries, and low for the rest of the African region and globally.

Ituri province remains the most affected, with 2,160 cases including 811 deaths, reported from 28 of 36 health zones (up from 27/36); North Kivu has reported 239 cases including 141 deaths from 11 of 34 health zones; South Kivu 3 cases including 1 death from 1 of 34 health zones; Haut-Uele 16 cases including 10 deaths from 4 of 13 health zones; and Tshopo 5 cases including 4 deaths from 3 of 23 health zones — 47 of 140 health zones affected in total, still across the same five provinces (no new province reported). Uganda has reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths, with the last confirmed case on 21 June and no new cases since; its last patient was discharged on 16 July, and the 42-day countdown toward declaring Uganda's outbreak over is ongoing.

The outbreak is now the largest recorded Ebola virus disease outbreak in the country, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak (3,317 confirmed cases). On 28 July, Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the end of the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the country, following 42 days without a new confirmed locally transmitted case after the last confirmed case was discharged from care on 16 June 2026.

In total, 1481 confirmed cases; 1460 from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 20 from Uganda and one from France (linked to DRC); and 454 deaths including two from Uganda, have been reported. description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo declared its 17th Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus, on 15 May 2026, centred in Ituri Province. On 17 May the WHO Director-General determined that the DRC and Uganda epidemic constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). It remains the largest Ebola outbreak recorded in the country: ECDC's country overview (data as of 28 August 2026) reports 5,945 confirmed cases including 2,862 deaths in the DRC, spanning 60 of 151 health zones across six provinces, with 896 patients currently in isolation. Uganda's linked chain ended at 20 confirmed cases and two deaths -- first declared over by its own Ministry of Health on 28 July 2026, then formally declared over by WHO on 26 August 2026 after 42 days without a new case; imported cases were earlier confirmed in France and Germany. On 20 August 2026 WHO and Africa CDC announced the allocation of 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine to DRC, including 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing its efficacy against the Bundibugyo strain and 50,000 doses for frontline health workers; the DRC outbreak remains ongoing.

On 20 August 2026, WHO and Africa CDC announced the allocation of 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine to DRC -- 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial and 50,000 for frontline health workers -- though Ervebo's efficacy against the Bundibugyo strain driving this outbreak has not yet been established.
